## Stage 1 — Scaffold project and Notion API client
Depends on: none
Build a TypeScript command-line tool that syncs Notion pages to Markdown files. Create a repository with `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `src/`, `tests/`, and a `bin` entry. Use Node.js built-in modules and TypeScript only; avoid vendor-specific CLI frameworks. Implement a small config layer that reads `NOTION_TOKEN`, `NOTION_PAGE_ID`, output directory, and optional include/exclude filters from environment variables or a JSON config file. Implement `NotionClient` with `getPage`, `getBlockChildren`, and pagination. Use the Notion REST API directly with `fetch` and Notion version `2022-02-22`. Add typed interfaces for Notion page and block responses. Add error handling for missing token, 401/403/404, rate limiting, and malformed responses. Add unit tests for config loading and pagination using dependency injection or a mock fetch function. Acceptance: `build`, `test`, and `typecheck` scripts pass; no live network calls in tests.

## Stage 2 — Implement Notion block to Markdown conversion
Depends on: Stage 1
Extend the TypeScript CLI project from Stage 1. Implement a pure conversion module that turns Notion blocks into GitHub-flavored Markdown. Support paragraph, headings, bulleted list, numbered list, to_do, quote, callout, code, image, file, bookmark, divider, toggle, table, table_row, embed, audio, video, synced_block, and link_to_page. Recursively convert children and preserve nesting. Convert rich text with text, mentions, formulas, equations, and annotations: bold, italic, strikethrough, underline, code, and links. Escape Markdown control characters safely. Render code blocks with triple backticks and language. Render images and files as Markdown links or image syntax using the URL from the block. Render tables as GitHub-flavored Markdown tables. Write focused unit tests for each block type, nested lists, annotations, escaping, and table conversion. Acceptance: converter is deterministic, has no file or network side effects, and all Stage 2 tests pass.

## Stage 3 — Build sync engine and local Markdown writer
Depends on: Stage 1, Stage 2
Extend the project. Implement a sync engine that starts from a Notion page, fetches page metadata, recursively fetches child pages and blocks, converts blocks to Markdown, and writes files to a local output directory. Create a file path resolver that sanitizes page titles, keeps a stable unique suffix based on page id, and preserves page hierarchy as directories. Write Markdown files with YAML frontmatter containing id, title, source URL, parent id, last edited time, and sync time. Maintain a state file under the output directory with page id, path, last_edited_time, and content hash for incremental sync. Support dry-run mode that reports planned creates, updates, skips, and deletes without writing. Map links between synced pages to relative local Markdown links when possible, and leave external links unchanged. Add integration tests using a fake NotionClient that returns nested pages, collisions, unicode titles, and incremental updates. Acceptance: running sync writes a correct Markdown tree, state updates, and repeated sync with no changes produces no writes.

## Stage 4 — CLI commands, flags, and user experience
Depends on: Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3
Extend the TypeScript CLI. Implement a bin entry named `notion-md-sync` using `process.argv` and no vendor-specific CLI framework. Provide commands: `init` to write a starter config file, `sync` to run the sync engine, and `convert` to convert a single block JSON fixture for debugging. Accept flags: `--token`, `--page-id`, `--output`, `--dry-run`, `--clean`, `--verbose`, `--include`, and `--exclude`. Load configuration with precedence: CLI flags, environment variables, config file, defaults. Show a concise summary of fetched pages, written files, skipped files, deleted stale files, and errors. Use non-zero exit codes for fatal errors and handle Ctrl+C by aborting cleanly. Add CLI integration tests that invoke the command through dependency injection or a spawned process with a mock HTTP server or mock client. Acceptance: help text, missing token, invalid page id, dry-run, and successful sync paths are covered by tests.

## Stage 5 — Final tests, documentation, and acceptance
Depends on: Stage 1, Stage 2, Stage 3, Stage 4
Finish the TypeScript CLI that syncs Notion pages to Markdown files. Add a full test suite with unit tests for config, Notion client, converter, path resolver, writer, and sync engine; integration tests for nested page sync and incremental sync; and end-to-end CLI tests using a local fake Notion REST server or injected mock client. Ensure tests run offline and clean temporary output directories. Add `README.md` with installation, configuration, commands, examples, security notes about tokens, supported blocks, limitations around expired Notion file URLs, and troubleshooting. Add `AGENTS.md` or docs explaining architecture and how to add a new block converter. Ensure package scripts for `build`, `typecheck`, and `test` pass. Acceptance: a developer can configure a token and page id, run sync, obtain Markdown files with frontmatter and local links, rerun sync idempotently, and understand failures from CLI messages and tests.
